title: Technology Sector Update for 11/07/2018: MITK,TWLO,FIVN,MTCH
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT +3.87%
AAPL +2.48%
IBM +1.21%
CSCO +2.83%
GOOG +3.44%
Technology stocks soared today, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding about 2.7% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose almost 1.1%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Mitek Systems ( MITK ) was more than 2% lower in late Wednesday trading, reversing a more than 2% rise that followed erased almost all of its prior gains that followed the image capture and identity verification software firm announcing Max Carnecchia has been hired to be the new CEO, succeeding Jim DeBello. Carnecchia was most recently the CEO of Illuminate Education, a cloud-based student assessment and reporting platform.
In other sector news:
(+) Twilio ( TWLO ) rose to a new record high on Wednesday, climbing almost 37% to a best-ever $96.97 a share after the cloud communications company reported better-than-expected non-GAAP Q3 net income and revenue and guided for upbeat results for the current quarter ending Dec. 31. Excluding one-time items, it earned $0.07 per share, reversing an 0.08 per share net loss during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ by $0.05 per share. Revenue rose 68% year over year to $168.9 million, also surpassing the $151.6 million analyst mean. Looking forward, Twilio is projecting Q4 net income and revenue topping Street views by at least $0.01 per share and $22 million, respectively.
(+) Five9 ( FIVN ) jumped almost 17% higher on Wednesday after the cloud software company reported a more than fourfold rise in Q3 net income and a 30% increase over year-ago levels. It earned $0.18 per share during the three months ended Sept. 30, up from a $0.04 per share profit during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.09 per share. Revenue rose to $65.3 million from $50.1 million last year and topped the Street view by $0.09 per share. It raised its FY18 earnings outlook by 23.5% and its revenue guidance by 2.5% at their respective mid-points to a new range of $0.49 to $0.51 per share on between $251.1 to $252.2 million versus the consensus view expecting net income of $0.39 to $0.42 per share on $244.5 million to $246.5 million in revenue.
(-) Match Group ( MTCH ) declined almost 21% at one point on Wednesday after revenue growth for the online-dating platform slowed compared with the prior quarter, upstaging Q3 net income and revenue topping analyst forecasts. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.39 per share, more than doubling its $0.19 per share non-GAAP profit during the same quarter last year and beating analyst estimates by $0.03 per share. Revenue rose 29.2% year-over-year to $443.9 million compared with 53% growth during the April-to-June reporting period.
